AboveHighestBand.description:
What a party above the highest band costs, or that it is refused, chosen
by its `type` member.

BandedInput.description: The closed input set a banded table may read. Tier 1 reads exactly one.

CalendarExceptionRecord.description:
An owned dated exception over local wall-clock time, the record form of
`registry_platform_calendar::CalendarException`. An exception is scoped to
one location: a closure at one counter never closes another.

location.description: The location this exception applies to.

Channel.description: The authenticated channel a subquota limits.

ExceptionRecordKind.description: The layer an exception occupies, mirrored for records.

FixtureAdmissionRequest.description:
One replayed request as an author writes it.

This is the authoring form of an admission request, not the wire form. It
carries everything the wire request carries plus `rescheduleOf`, the claim
this case replaces: a fixture legitimately says "this case reschedules that
one", where an HTTP caller may not, because on the wire the exclusion is
the runtime's to supply from inside its own transaction.

capabilities.description:
The capabilities the party holds. A party holding none omits the
member.

channel.description:
The channel the caller books through. It is free text so a fixture
can exercise the refusal of a channel outside the vocabulary.

policyRevision.description:
The policy revision the caller resolved the offering under. Replay
runs the policy at revision 1.

prerequisites.description:
The prerequisites the party holds. A party holding none omits the
member.

rescheduleOf.description:
The claim this case replaces. Its allocation is left out of this
case's conflict checks and removed when the case is admitted, so a
reschedule never competes with what it replaces. A claim an earlier
case booked is `case:` followed by that case's name.

FixtureCase.description: One replayed request and its expectation.

name.description:
The case name, which also identifies the claim an admitted case
records.

FixtureExpectation.description: One case's expected outcome, chosen by its `type` member.

resource.description:
The pool member an exact-time case lands on. Omit it to accept
any member.

code.description: A public problem code, exactly as a caller would receive it.

FixtureParty.description:
The party one replayed case requests for. Zero is allowed in both counts
so a fixture can exercise the refusal of a party the offering cannot
serve.

LedgerClaim.description:
One entry in the authoritative supply ledger.

`start` and `end` are the occupied interval including any setup and cleanup
buffers, so two claims that merely touch at their displayed times still
conflict when their buffers overlap.

channel.description:
The authenticated channel the claim was allocated in, when the supply
carries channel subquotas.

duplicateKey.description:
The duplicate-active key this claim holds, when the offering defines
one.

expiresAt.description:
Hold expiry. An expired hold stops consuming capacity at this instant
even when the cleanup worker is delayed.

offering.description: The offering whose duplicate-active policy owns this claim.

supplyId.description:
The pool member resource (exact time) or the window (arrival) this
claim occupies.

units.description: Recipient units consumed. Exact-time claims on one member consume one.

LedgerKind.description: What a ledger entry allocates supply for.

LeftoverCapacityPolicy.description:
What a window says happens to its leftover capacity when it closes. The
declaration names an intent; this version of the runtime reads none of
it, so `check` refuses a window that declares one rather than accept a
promise nothing keeps. There is no default and no borrowing from the
next window.

oneOf.description: Leftover units would lapse with the window.
Leftover units would become available to the walk-in channel.

LocalId.description: A local identifier: a lowercase letter, then up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, `_`, or `-`.

LocationRecord.description:
A location record: the layer of configuration an operator maintains at
runtime, not inside the authored policy.

timezone.description: A named IANA timezone such as `Asia/Bangkok`.

PoolMember.description:
One interchangeable member of a resource pool.

`available` carries no reason. Why a member is unavailable is private staff
information; the public answer to a caller is that capacity is exhausted.

capabilities.description:
The capabilities this member carries. Omitted or `[]`, it carries
none and serves only offerings that require none.

PublishedWindow.description: A published arrival window with its capacity.

leftover.description:
Declared intent for the window's leftover capacity. Nothing reads it
in this version, so a declaration is refused at authoring; the field
stays so a refusal can name it.

subquotas.description:
Per-channel ceilings within `units`. A window that limits no channel
omits the member.

units.description: Published capacity in the unit basis the units policy defines.

RequiredUnitsPolicy.description:
How an offering converts a party into consumed recipient units, chosen by
its `type` member.

oneOf.description: Every party costs the same fixed units.
A party costs its recipient count times `per_recipient`.
A party costs whatever band its recipient count falls in.

ResourcePool.description:
A pool of interchangeable resources backing exact-time offerings. A pool is
its concrete members, never an independent counter.

SchedulingFacts.description:
The environment records an admission runs against: locations, pools,
published windows, and dated exceptions. In production these are runtime records; in an offline
replay they are fixture facts. The evaluator never reads or mutates them
directly; its caller resolves them into the context the evaluator takes.
A fixture may omit an empty collection; replay fails fast when a case
references a record the facts do not carry.

windows.description:
Published arrival-window supply owned by this deployment's operator
records. The policy references these records by identifier.

UnitBand.description:
One band of a banded units table: parties up to `up_to` recipients cost
`units`.

WindowStaffing.description:
The staffing block a window's supply is carved from, when the window is
backed by the same concrete resources an exact-time pool sells.

A pool that backs a window may not also back an exact-time offering: a
window claim occupies the window's own supply while an exact-time claim
occupies the member it books, so the two modes would double-book the same
staffing in a ledger that cannot see the conflict. That mix is refused at
publication whatever this block declares.

`reserved_members` records how many pool members the window's supply is
intended to use. The current ledger does not enforce that partition between
windows, so two windows backed by the same pool may not overlap, whatever
either staffing block declares. Disjoint windows may reuse the pool.

WindowSubquota.description: A per-channel ceiling within a window's published capacity.

description: An offline replay fixture: synthetic facts, a starting ledger, and cases.

initial.description:
The claims the ledger holds before the first case. A fixture that
starts from an empty ledger omits the member.

now.description: The single observed instant every case runs at.
